title: Planning a speech solution · Level 3
slo: Assess the main requirements before adding speech to an application.

exercises.question_text: What should a team verify for language and dialect support? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Support must include the languages users need. Language requirements differ across languages.
Regional variations are dialects. A team should verify that required dialects are supported.
For spoken input, the capability must understand the required languages and variations. Support should be checked before implementation.

options.error_type: Confuses language support with audio quality
options.rationale: Microphone distance affects captured audio quality. It does not determine which languages or dialects are supported.
options.better_fit: Use this when assessing audio capture conditions for recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: A suitable microphone position would not add support for a needed regional variation.
feedback.instructional: Language support concerns what people speak; microphone distance concerns how clearly speech is captured.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Verify the target languages, regional variations, and the ability to handle them.

exercises.question_text: Which planning area covers how audio is stored and protected?

options.rationale: Privacy and compliance cover how audio is processed, stored, protected, and regulated. This is the planning area for data handling.

options.error_type: Confuses data protection with audio conditions
options.rationale: Audio quality concerns noise, microphones, distance, and bandwidth. It does not cover storage or protection of audio data.
options.better_fit: Use this when assessing noise or microphone quality.

feedback.intrinsic: The recording may be clear while its handling still fails to protect sensitive information.
feedback.instructional: Choose privacy and compliance for questions about processing, storage, and protection.

options.error_type: Confuses data protection with language support
options.rationale: Language support concerns target languages and regional speech variations. It does not describe how audio data is protected.
options.better_fit: Use this when checking supported speech variations.

feedback.intrinsic: Supporting a caller's dialect would not answer how their audio is stored safely.
feedback.instructional: Keep language support separate from privacy obligations.

options.error_type: Confuses data protection with processing delay
options.rationale: Latency is the delay between input and output. It does not address data storage or protection.
options.better_fit: Use this when setting response-time needs.

feedback.intrinsic: Fast responses would not protect audio that is handled improperly.
feedback.instructional: Latency concerns timing; privacy and compliance concern responsible audio-data handling.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Privacy and compliance address how audio data is handled and protected.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Long pauses can make a live exchange feel slow and interrupt the flow of conversation.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Real-time conversations need low latency, while batch transcription can tolerate more delay.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Low latency helps a live conversation feel responsive.

exercises.question_text: Which conditions can affect recognition accuracy? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Noise can interfere with captured speech. It can reduce recognition accuracy.
Microphone quality affects the captured audio. Clearer capture supports more accurate recognition.
Distance from the speaker affects the audio reaching the microphone. This can affect downstream accuracy.
Beam width belongs to decoding, where possible transcriptions are searched. It is not an audio capture condition.
options.better_fit: Use this when balancing decoding accuracy with speed in recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: Improving decoding choices will not fix speech that was poorly captured at the microphone.
feedback.instructional: Focus on noise, microphone quality, and speaker distance when judging audio conditions.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Background noise, microphone quality, and speaker distance all affect how clearly speech is captured.

exercises.question_text: Which approach fits an application that needs to understand spoken commands?

options.rationale: Speech recognition converts spoken words into written text. It fits an application that must understand spoken commands.

options.error_type: Confuses spoken input with spoken output
options.rationale: Speech synthesis converts written text into spoken audio. It does not turn a spoken command into text.
options.better_fit: Use this when text must be spoken aloud.

feedback.intrinsic: The application could speak a reply but would not capture what the person said.
feedback.instructional: Use recognition for spoken input and synthesis for spoken output.

options.error_type: Confuses solution selection with a synthesis stage
options.rationale: Text normalization prepares written text for pronunciation in speech synthesis. It is not the capability for understanding spoken commands.
options.better_fit: Use this when preparing written text for pronunciation.

feedback.intrinsic: The application may prepare outgoing text well while the spoken command remains unrecognized.
feedback.instructional: Text normalization is one synthesis stage; speech recognition handles incoming spoken words.

options.error_type: Confuses solution selection with a recognition stage
options.rationale: Beam search is a decoding technique that selects a likely transcription. It is not the overall capability selected for spoken input.
options.better_fit: Use this when selecting the best transcription during recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: Choosing this stage alone would not describe the full approach needed for voice commands.
feedback.instructional: Select speech recognition for the capability; beam search is one part of its decoding process.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech recognition converts spoken input into text so commands can be understood.

exercises.question_text: A real-time conversation needs low ___ so responses arrive quickly.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: People may experience a noticeable pause before the reply arrives.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use latency. Audio quality affects clarity, and beam search is a decoding technique; neither names response delay.

exercises.explanation: Low latency means little delay between input and output. That is why it matters for a real-time conversation.

exercises.question_text: Speech synthesis is the right capability when an application must convert spoken commands into text.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A person could speak a command, but the application would not have the text needed to understand it.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Match recognition to spoken input. Match speech synthesis, also called text-to-speech, to spoken output.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech recognition converts spoken commands into text; synthesis creates spoken audio from text.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The cause and its effect are unclear, making it harder to identify what needs attention.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Put the audio condition first, followed by what it can confuse and when.

exercises.correct_answer: Background noise can confuse the recognition model before later processing
exercises.explanation: The sentence first names the audio condition, then explains its effect. Noise can confuse recognition before later processing.

exercises.question_text: What does language and dialect support mean?

options.text: Supporting target languages and regional speech variations
options.rationale: This describes support for the languages users need and their regional variations. That is the meaning of language and dialect support.

options.error_type: Confuses language support with audio filtering
options.rationale: Removing hums is audio filtering before recognition. It does not address what languages or dialects can be handled.
options.better_fit: Use this when improving audio before recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: The recording may become cleaner without meeting users' language needs.
feedback.instructional: Filtering handles unwanted sounds; language and dialect support handles speech variations.

options.rationale: Reducing delay concerns latency between input and output. It does not provide language or dialect support.
options.better_fit: Use this when planning a live conversation.

feedback.intrinsic: A quick response may still fail to handle the language a caller speaks.
feedback.instructional: Latency is timing; language and dialect support is about speech variations.

options.rationale: Formatting raw text is post-processing after transcription. It does not determine whether a language variation is supported.
options.better_fit: Use this when making a transcript easier to read.

feedback.intrinsic: The team could format transcripts well while users' regional speech remains unsupported.
feedback.instructional: Language support must be verified before implementation, not added through transcript formatting.

exercises.explanation: Correct. It means handling the target languages and the regional ways people speak them.

exercises.question_text: Which questions belong to privacy and compliance planning? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Processing audio data is part of privacy and compliance planning. Teams need to understand how it is handled.
Storage of audio data is a privacy concern. Teams should understand it before implementation.
Protecting audio data is central to privacy and compliance. This is especially important for sensitive information.
Dialect support concerns regional speech variations. It is separate from how audio data is handled and protected.
options.better_fit: Use this when planning language and dialect support.

feedback.intrinsic: The team may know the right dialect but still leave sensitive audio handling unexamined.
feedback.instructional: Ask about processing, storage, and protection when planning privacy and compliance.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These questions address how audio data is handled, stored, and protected.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The team may not clearly see what must be checked before beginning the work.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with verification, name both language needs, and end with the timing.

exercises.correct_answer: Verify support for target languages and regional dialects before implementation
exercises.explanation: The action is to verify support before work begins. The support must cover both target languages and regional dialects.

exercises.question_text: Privacy and compliance require teams to understand how audio data is processed, stored, and ___.

parts.text: Privacy and compliance require teams to understand how audio data is processed, stored, and

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Audio information may be handled without adequate safeguards, particularly when it is sensitive.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use protected. Teams must understand how audio is processed, stored, and protected.

exercises.explanation: Privacy planning includes safeguarding audio data throughout its handling. Decoding and sampling are processing activities, not the protection requirement.
